title: Aavaas
transcript: So most people walk into an architect's office with a plot size, a Pinterest board, and no idea what they actually want, and pay in months of revisions to find out. The product turns that first conversation into a working model before the appointment. You describe the plot, the road, the family, and how you live. If you are into Vastu, uh, If you are into Vastu, you share your, uh, preferences. You share the direction of your plot, the facing of your plot, and, uh, in plain language, all of it in plain language. It asks the questions an architect, a senior architect, would ask you. Which way does it face? Who sleeps where? How many cars do you want? Do you follow Vastu or not? Then it draws you floor plans. You can argue with. You can actually come back any number of times you want for those floor plans. And then it builds the house as a 3D model you can spin like a dollhouse, lift floor by floor, and walk through at eye height from the gate to the roof. Change your mind about the kitchen and the model changes with you. What you take to the architect is not a blank slate. But a plan you have stood inside, you have roamed inside, you have checked every inch of it inside, with the reasons for each design written down so the professional's time goes into making it buildable rather than guessing what you actually want. Why it works and what it doesn't— the value is in the reasoning layer, not the renderer. Room sizes that are honest about the plot, parking that respects the road, Orientation and Vastu placements, the trade-offs said out loud. So yeah.

prd.oneLiner: Aavaas turns the first plot-and-family conversation into a walkable, arguable 3D home model with written design reasoning — where GrehYug and Cadbull hand you a one-shot Vastu plan and Architects House hands you a preset catalog.
prd.problem: People walk into an architect's office with a plot size, a Pinterest board, and no real idea of what they want, then pay in months of revisions to discover it — the transcript describes this exact blind first meeting as the industry norm. Today's coping mechanism is either hiring an architect cold and iterating expensively, or using AI generators like GrehYug, Cadbull, or Naksha that take a static form (plot, facing, BHK, Vastu toggle) and spit out a one-shot plan for a flat fee, with no room to argue with it and no explanation of why any room sits where it does. Architect-catalog platforms like Architects House solve speed with presets, but you're customizing someone else's archetype, not designing from how your family actually lives. The gap the market leaves open: no tool treats the brief as a conversation about lifestyle, lets you revise for free until it's right, or hands the architect a walkable model with the reasoning already written down — so the professional's time still goes into guessing instead of building.
prd.targetUser: First-time Indian homeowners with an owned residential plot who are about to engage — or are already stuck revising with — an architect, and want to arrive at that meeting with a reasoned, walkable plan instead of a blank brief.

research.marketSummary: India's residential pre-architect design space is rapidly filling with AI floor plan generators, splitting into three clusters: (1) Vastu-first tools (GrehYug, Cadbull, Naksha) that generate compliant 2D/3D plans from plot+facing inputs at low cost but treat Vastu and lifestyle as checkbox inputs rather than a conversational reasoning process; (2) architect-catalog platforms (Architects House) that offer curated archetypes with budget/render bundles but start from presets rather than a truly bespoke brief; (3) general-purpose 2D-to-3D visualization tools (HouseGPTs, DesignDrafter) aimed at broader design/drafting use cases without India-specific regulatory or Vastu depth. Nearly all treat 'generate a plan' as a single-shot transaction rather than an iterative, walkable, argued-with negotiation between homeowner and system, and none document design reasoning in a form built for an architect handoff.
research.ourPositioning: Unlike single-shot Vastu generators or architect catalogs that hand you a plan, we turn the first conversation into a living, walkable model you can argue with endlessly and take to your architect already reasoned-through — collapsing months of blind revisions into a single informed first meeting.

engineering.overview: Aavaas is a web application that converts a conversational plot-and-lifestyle intake into a rule-validated floor plan, a spinnable 3D dollhouse model, a PDF export, and written design rationale. The system combines an LLM-driven conversational intake layer, a deterministic Vastu/setback rules engine, a layout generation service that produces structured room geometry, and a client-side 3D renderer that consumes that geometry. Users can iterate on the intake and regenerate plans for free, with each iteration versioned so they can compare and revert. A single checkout unlocks the final downloadable package (PDF + rationale + 3D export).
engineering.dataFlow: User signs in → creates a Project → Conversational Intake UI collects plot/facing/family/Vastu answers, sent to Intake Orchestration Service which structures and stores them as intake_responses → on 'generate', Floor Plan Generation Engine reads intake_responses + plot data, applies Vastu & Setback Rules Engine to produce a versioned floor_plans record with nested rooms → Design Rationale Generator attaches rationale_text per room/category → 3D Model Service converts layout_json into a model asset consumed by the browser-side Three.js viewer; PDF Export Service renders the same layout_json into a PDF stored in Supabase Storage → user reviews the dollhouse model and PDF, can revise intake (creating a new floor_plan version) at no cost → once satisfied, user completes checkout (Orders) which unlocks final downloadable assets.

components.name: Conversational Intake UI
components.responsibility: Guides the user through plain-language questions about plot, facing, family composition, sleeping arrangements, parking, and Vastu preference; stores structured answers incrementally.

components.name: Intake Orchestration Service (LLM)
components.responsibility: Uses an LLM to turn free-text/guided answers into structured intake fields, ask clarifying follow-ups, and detect when enough information exists to generate a plan.

components.name: Floor Plan Generation Engine
components.responsibility: Combines plot geometry, BHK requirements, and intake data with the Vastu/setback rules engine to produce a structured room-by-room layout (positions, dimensions, zones).

components.name: Vastu & Setback Rules Engine
components.responsibility: Deterministic rule set (strict/light/none Vastu modes, municipal setback norms by road width) that validates and adjusts room placement produced by the generation engine.

components.name: Design Rationale Generator (LLM)
components.responsibility: Generates one-line written reasoning per major room/trade-off decision (orientation, Vastu, parking, climate) tied to the layout output.

components.name: 3D Model Service
components.responsibility: Converts the structured layout JSON into a renderable 3D scene definition (walls, floors, room volumes) consumed by a client-side Three.js/React-Three-Fiber viewer for spin/floor-lift interaction.

components.name: PDF Export Service
components.responsibility: Renders the 2D floor plan, dimensions, Vastu zones, and rationale notes into a downloadable PDF.

components.name: Revision & Versioning Service
components.responsibility: Tracks intake edits and regenerated floor plan versions per project, enabling free unlimited iteration and rollback.

components.name: Payments & Checkout
components.responsibility: Handles the single paid checkout that unlocks final PDF/3D export downloads.

components.name: Auth & Profile Service
components.responsibility: Manages user sign-up/login and project ownership via Supabase Auth.

components.name: Storage
components.responsibility: Stores generated PDFs, 3D model assets, and intermediate layout artifacts in Supabase Storage.

techStack.llm: OpenAI GPT-4o (or equivalent) used for: (1) conversational intake structuring/follow-up questions, (2) assisting layout heuristics alongside the deterministic Vastu/setback rules engine, (3) generating one-line design rationale text.
techStack.auth: Supabase Auth (email/password + OAuth) with RLS policies tying rows to auth.uid().
techStack.infra: Vercel for frontend/API hosting, Supabase Storage for PDF and 3D asset files, Supabase Postgres managed DB.
techStack.backend: Next.js API Routes / Supabase Edge Functions for orchestration (intake processing, layout generation, rationale generation, PDF rendering, checkout webhooks).
techStack.database: Supabase Postgres with Row Level Security scoped per user_id/project_id.
techStack.devtools: TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, Zod for schema validation, GitHub Actions for CI (lint/typecheck/test), Vercel Preview Deployments.
techStack.frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router) + React + TypeScript + TailwindCSS; React-Three-Fiber/Three.js for the spinnable 3D dollhouse viewer; React Hook Form + Zod for the conversational intake steps.

tasks.title: Auth setup

tasks.title: Deploy setup
tasks.description: Configure Vercel project with Supabase environment variables, set up preview/production environments, and connect GitHub Actions for lint/typecheck/build checks on PRs before merge.

tasks.title: Conversational Plot & Lifestyle Intake flow
tasks.description: Build the guided Q&A UI capturing plot dimensions, facing, road width, family composition, sleeping arrangements, parking needs, and Vastu preference; persist answers incrementally as intake_responses tied to a project.

tasks.title: Floor Plan Generation Engine
tasks.description: Implement the service that takes intake_responses + plot geometry, applies the Vastu & Setback Rules Engine (strict/light/none modes, road-width-based setbacks), and produces a versioned floor_plans record with associated rooms.

tasks.title: Design Rationale Generation
tasks.description: Integrate LLM call that reads the generated layout_json and produces one-line rationale_text entries per room/category (orientation, vastu, parking, climate, family), stored in design_rationales.

tasks.title: 3D Dollhouse Model Viewer
tasks.description: Build a service that converts floor plan layout_json into a 3D scene definition (per-floor room volumes) and a React-Three-Fiber viewer supporting spin and floor-lift interactions.

tasks.title: 2D Floor Plan PDF Export
tasks.description: Implement server-side PDF rendering of the current floor plan (room layout, dimensions, Vastu zones, rationale notes) and store the file in Supabase Storage, linked via floor_plans.pdf_url.

tasks.title: Free Revision Loop & Versioning
tasks.description: Allow users to edit intake answers and regenerate the floor plan without cost, creating a new floor_plans version and a revisions log entry while marking the previous version is_current = false.

tasks.title: Checkout & Order Fulfillment
tasks.description: Integrate a single payment provider (e.g. Razorpay) to unlock final downloadable PDF/3D exports upon successful payment, recording the transaction in orders and updating project.status to 'paid'.

openQuestions: What minimum 3D fidelity (static dollhouse vs. eye-height walkthrough) is achievable given the chosen rendering stack and build timeline?

Should floor plan geometry generation rely primarily on deterministic rule-based logic or LLM-assisted layout reasoning, and how do we validate LLM-produced geometry doesn't violate physical/Vastu constraints?
How do we source and encode setback/municipal bylaw data per city/state for the Vastu & Setback Rules Engine within the MVP timeline?
What format should model_assets use for the 3D scene (custom JSON consumed directly by Three.js vs. exporting to glTF) to balance generation simplicity and rendering fidelity?
Should Vastu compliance be surfaced as a numeric score or narrative-only rationale, and how does that decision affect the design_rationales schema?
What is the versioning/storage strategy for repeated free regenerations to avoid unbounded storage growth of PDFs and 3D assets per project?
Which payment provider (Razorpay, Stripe) best supports INR checkout and webhook reliability for the single paid unlock flow?
engineering.schemaSqlExcerpt:
CREATE TABLE projects (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  plot_width numeric,
  plot_length numeric,
  facing text,
  road_width numeric,
  vastu_preference text CHECK (vastu_preference IN ('strict','light','none')) DEFAULT 'light',
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','generated','paid')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE floor_plans (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  project_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  version int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  bhk_count int,
  layout_json jsonb NOT NULL,
  is_current boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);
